1.w: So get rid of all evil and all deceit and hypocrisy and envy and all slander.

2.w: And yearn like newborn infants for pure, spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up to salvation,

3.w: if you have experienced the Lord’s kindness.

4.w: So as you come to him, a living stone rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight,

5.w: you yourselves, as living stones, are built up as a spiritual house to be a holy priesthood and to offer spiritual sacrifices that are acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

6.w: For it says in scripture, “Look, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone, and whoever believes in him will never be put to shame.”

7.w: So you who believe see his value, but for those who do not believe, the stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,

8.w: and a stumbling-stone and a rock to trip over. They stumble because they disobey the word, as they were destined to do.

9.w: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people of his own, so that you may proclaim the virtues of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.

10.w: You once were not a people, but now you are God’s people. You were shown no mercy, but now you have received mercy.

11.w: Dear friends, I urge you as foreigners and exiles to keep away from fleshly desires that do battle against the soul,

12.w: and maintain good conduct among the non-Christians, so that though they now malign you as wrongdoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God when he appears.

13.w: Be subject to every human institution for the Lord’s sake, whether to a king as supreme

14.w: or to governors as those he commissions to punish wrongdoers and praise those who do good.

15.w: For God wants you to silence the ignorance of foolish people by doing good.

16.w: Live as free people, not using your freedom as a pretext for evil, but as God’s slaves.

17.w: Honor all people, love the family of believers, fear God, honor the king.

18.w: Slaves, be subject to your masters with all reverence, not only to those who are good and gentle, but also to those who are perverse.

19.w: For this finds God’s favor, if because of conscience toward God someone endures hardships in suffering unjustly.

20.w: For what credit is it if you sin and are mistreated and endure it? But if you do good and suffer and so endure, this finds favor with God.

21.w: For to this you were called, since Christ also suffered for you, leaving an example for you to follow in his steps.

22.w: He committed no sin nor was deceit found in his mouth.

23.w: When he was maligned, he did not answer back; when he suffered, he threatened no retaliation, but committed himself to God who judges justly.

24.w: He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we may cease from sinning and live for righteousness. By his wounds you were healed.

25.w: For you were going astray like sheep but now you have turned back to the shepherd and guardian of your souls.
